meta.title: Source conflict register
meta.rule: When two sources give different values for the same measure and period, both are shown. We never average them or pick a winner without evidence. Explanations below are hypotheses, labelled as such, until a reviewer confirms them against the original pages.
meta.reviewed: Not yet reviewed by a subject specialist

values.label: FY 2023/24 report
FY 2024/25 report (quoted as prior year)

conflicts.definitions: The FY 2023/24 report splits its figure into health facility financing (KSh 388.53m) and ordinary own-source revenue (KSh 222.10m). The FY 2024/25 report does not give a split for the prior year.
conflicts.hypothesis: The later report may restate the year or count a different scope. The gap is not explained by facility income alone: 610.74 minus 388.53 is 222.21, not 427.95.
conflicts.effect: 610.74 is plotted as the main value and 427.95 as the other report's value (hollow marker). The Insights page states the disagreement beside the chart; treat the FY 2023/24 and FY 2024/25 own-source revenue comparison as uncertain.

values.label: FY 2016/17 report (text)
FY 2018/19 report (chart)

conflicts.definitions: Both are described as the county's own revenue for the year. The FY 2015/16 report itself gives 127.93, of which 120.44 was deposited into the County Revenue Fund.
conflicts.hypothesis: The later chart may be a restated series that excludes revenue spent at source.
conflicts.effect: 127.93 is plotted, with 113.26 shown as the other report's value.

values.label: FY 2014/15 report
FY 2018/19 report (chart)

conflicts.definitions: Both describe the county's own revenue for the year.
conflicts.hypothesis: The difference is small and may be rounding or a minor restatement.
conflicts.effect: Immaterial to any trend statement. 143.33 is plotted.

values.label: FY 2020/21 report
FY 2021/22 report (opening stock)

conflicts.definitions: The FY 2020/21 report states recurrent KSh 637.54m plus development KSh 423.38m. The FY 2021/22 report states recurrent KSh 250.51m plus development KSh 351.58m as the stock outstanding on the same date.
conflicts.hypothesis: The later report may count only bills verified as eligible, or use a different cut-off. The reports do not say.
conflicts.effect: Each year's pending-bills column uses the figure from that year's report where one is readable, and the register lists every case where another report differs. The rise over ten years should be read as a direction, not as exact steps.

values.label: Budget financing table (own-source target)
Implied by the stated 47 per cent (436.68 / 0.47)

conflicts.definitions: KSh 436.68m collected against 1,043m would be 41.9 per cent, but the report states 47 per cent.
conflicts.hypothesis: The two figures may measure different concepts (for example, budget financing versus the annual revenue target). The report does not explain.
conflicts.effect: The 47 per cent is quoted as the report's own statement and is not recomputed.

values.label: Report states
Recomputed (4.99 / 6.07)

conflicts.definitions: The recomputed value uses the approved recurrent budget of KSh 6.07bn.
conflicts.hypothesis: The report may use a revised budget as its denominator.
conflicts.effect: The report's stated 83 per cent is used and the recomputed 82.2 per cent is recorded here and in the year's note on the Data page.

values.label: Report text
Report table

conflicts.definitions: Within the same report. The table figure, with development spending of KSh 1.98bn, adds to the stated total of KSh 5.63bn.
conflicts.hypothesis: The text may be a typographical error or use a different measure.
conflicts.effect: The table value is used because it is consistent with the stated total.

values.label: FY 2022/23 report
FY 2023/24 report (quoted as prior year)

conflicts.definitions: Both are described as the approved supplementary budget for FY 2022/23.
conflicts.hypothesis: The later report may quote a different supplementary budget or round differently.
conflicts.effect: The FY 2022/23 report's own figure is used. The difference changes budget-spent shares by under one percentage point.

values.label: FY 2023/24 report (opening stock)
Auditor-General report, FY 2022/23
Controller of Budget FY 2022/23 report, closing stock in section 3.38.5 (PDF p. 578, printed p. 552, RapidOCR)

conflicts.definitions: The Controller of Budget figure is the opening stock quoted in the FY 2023/24 report. The Auditor-General reports the amount as an emphasis-of-matter item in the FY 2022/23 audit.
conflicts.hypothesis: Different cut-off dates or verification of bills. The reports do not say.
conflicts.effect: The chart plots 761.29, quoted from the later report because the FY 2022/23 report was not readable for this item. The difference is about 3 per cent.

values.label: FY 2024/25 report (opening stock)
FY 2023/24 report

conflicts.definitions: The FY 2023/24 report states KSh 303.91m outstanding at 30 June 2024 but says this excludes bills incurred during the year. The FY 2024/25 report gives the stock at 30 June 2024 as KSh 1.12 billion.
conflicts.hypothesis: The difference of about 3.7 times is probably a definition difference (bills incurred in the year included or not). The reports do not confirm this.
conflicts.effect: The chart and headline use 1,120 from the FY 2024/25 report. Because of the gap, the FY 2023/24 jump in pending bills is shown with this caveat and should not be read as a precise rise.

values.label: FY 2014/15 report text
FY 2018/19 report (chart)

conflicts.definitions: Both describe the county's own revenue for the 16 months to 30 June 2014.
conflicts.hypothesis: The difference of KSh 0.01 million is rounding.
conflicts.effect: Immaterial. 99.77 is plotted.

values.label: Controller of Budget FY 2020/21 report (quoted as prior year, PDF p. 374)
Siaya County Budget Review and Outlook Paper FY 2019/20 (county document, PDF p. 15)

conflicts.definitions: The county paper gives KSh 184,249,748 against a target of KSh 420m (43.87 per cent). The Controller of Budget figure is a comparison figure in the next year's report; that report does not say what it includes.
conflicts.hypothesis: Hypothesis: the two may count different revenue streams or be cut at different dates. The county paper is not an independent review.
conflicts.effect: 179.43 (Controller of Budget) is plotted as the main value and 184.25 as the other source's value (hollow marker). The county paper's other FY 2019/20 figures are listed but not plotted.

conflicts.measure: Cash balance brought forward from FY 2019/20 into FY 2020/21

values.label: Controller of Budget FY 2020/21 annual report, Table 3.215, actual (PDF p. 373)
Controller of Budget First Half FY 2020/21 report (PDF p. 319)

conflicts.definitions: The annual report gives KSh 1,186,274,440 actual against KSh 1,235,985,311 budgeted. The first-half report gives KSh 1,840,119,055 as both budget and actual.
conflicts.hypothesis: Hypothesis: the first-half figure may be an early estimate later restated, or the two may count different accounts. Neither report explains the difference.
conflicts.effect: Neither value is plotted; FY 2019/20 has no cash or balance series. Both are listed on the Data page.

values.label: Siaya County Budget Review and Outlook Paper FY 2019/20, supplementary budget (county document, PDF p. 11)
Auditor-General basis for opinion FY 2019/20, as reproduced by the Senate County Public Accounts Committee (PDF p. 517)

conflicts.definitions: Both documents describe a cut of KSh 341,576,215. The county paper applies it to an original budget of KSh 9,223,350,139 (giving 8,881,773,924). The audit gives a final budget of KSh 8,106,977,580 under exchequer releases and calls the cut unsupported.
conflicts.hypothesis: Hypothesis: the audit figure may be budgeted exchequer releases only, excluding items such as the balance brought forward, so it may not be the whole budget. Not confirmed.
conflicts.effect: Neither value is plotted: the Controller of Budget figure for FY 2019/20 is missing and stays a gap in the ten-year series.

conflicts.measure: County Assembly trade payables at 1 July 2025 (opening balance, FY 2025/26)

values.label: Controller of Budget First Quarter FY 2025/26 report, Table 3.436 (PDF p. 530)
Controller of Budget First Half FY 2025/26 report, text (PDF p. 223)

conflicts.definitions: Same date, same entity. The first-quarter table gives KSh 39,285,727; the first-half text gives "Kshs.72 million". Executive opening payables agree (KSh 1.89bn and 1.88bn).
conflicts.hypothesis: Hypothesis: the first-half report may include a later restatement or a different class of Assembly payables. Not confirmed; both read from scanned pages.
conflicts.effect: Both values are shown side by side in the in-year table on the Siaya hub. In-year figures are not part of the ten-year series.

conflicts.measure: Revenue arrears owed to the county, latest in-year figure, FY 2025/26

values.label: Controller of Budget First Quarter FY 2025/26 report, at 30 September 2025 (PDF p. 529)
Controller of Budget First Half FY 2025/26 report, Table 3.561, at 31 December 2025 (PDF p. 222)

conflicts.definitions: Different dates and a different scope. The first-quarter figure covers ordinary own-source revenue and facility improvement fund arrears only. The first-half figure adds KSh 620.36m of equitable share due for December; its own-source (KSh 45m) and facility fund (KSh 287m) parts are the same as at 30 September (derived: 45 plus 287 is 332).
conflicts.hypothesis: Hypothesis: the jump is mostly the newly included equitable share, and the unchanged own-source and facility fund parts may have been carried forward rather than re-counted. Not confirmed.
conflicts.effect: Both values are shown side by side, with their dates, in the in-year table on the Siaya hub. Do not read the rise from 332 to 953.73 as new arrears of the same kind.

conflicts.measure: Development absorption, FY 2022/23 (share of the annual development budget spent)

values.label: Controller of Budget FY 2022/23 report, department table total (PDF p. 583, printed p. 557, RapidOCR)
Same report, text of section 3.38.4 (PDF p. 578, printed p. 552, text layer and RapidOCR agree)

conflicts.definitions: Same report, same measure. The table total is 1,520.28 of 2,827.00 million, which is 53.8 per cent; the text says 53.4 per cent.
conflicts.hypothesis: Hypothesis: a typing slip in the text. Not confirmed.
conflicts.effect: The series keeps 53.8 (the table total, which matches the arithmetic). The text value is listed here.

conflicts.measure: Recurrent absorption, FY 2023/24 (share of the annual recurrent budget spent), as read from the scanned report

values.label: Controller of Budget FY 2023/24 report, section 3.38.4, PDF text layer (PDF p. 513, printed p. 490)
Same line read with RapidOCR at 200 to 400 dpi, and the department table total (PDF p. 517, printed p. 494)

conflicts.definitions: A reading conflict, not two sources: the PDF is a scan, and its embedded text layer and RapidOCR read the printed figure differently. The department table (5,138.67 of 5,909.25 million) gives 87.0 per cent by arithmetic.
conflicts.hypothesis: Hypothesis: the text layer misread 86.8 as 85.8, since two RapidOCR reads and the table agree on 86.8. Not confirmed against the page image.
conflicts.effect: The series still shows 85.8 until a reviewer checks the page image; both readings are listed here.

values.label: Controller of Budget FY 2023/24 report, section 3.38.4, PDF text layer (PDF p. 513, printed p. 490)
Same line read with RapidOCR at 200 to 400 dpi, and the department table total (PDF p. 517, printed p. 494)

conflicts.definitions: A reading conflict, not two sources (see recurrent-absorption-2023-24). The table (2,487.20 of 3,851.88 million) gives 64.6 per cent by arithmetic.
conflicts.hypothesis: Hypothesis: the text layer misread 64.6 as 64.5. Not confirmed against the page image.

values.label: Controller of Budget FY 2021/22 report, Table 3.251, column E (PDF p. 409, printed p. 385)
Controller of Budget FY 2022/23 report, opening stock for FY 2022/23 (PDF p. 578, printed p. 552, RapidOCR)

conflicts.definitions: The closing stock in one report and the opening stock in the next, for the same date.
conflicts.hypothesis: Hypothesis: the county revised its list of bills between the two reports (for example, bills verified later). The reports do not say. Not confirmed.
conflicts.effect: Both values are shown in the pending-bills roll-forward on the Insights page. The chart plots 705.38, the FY 2021/22 report's parts (411.53 development plus 293.85 recurrent).

conflicts.measure: Pending bills at 30 June 2022, within the FY 2021/22 report

values.label: Controller of Budget FY 2021/22 report, Table 3.251, column E (PDF p. 409, printed p. 385)
Same report, key observations (PDF p. 407, printed p. 383)

conflicts.definitions: Same report, same date. The table and the key observations give different totals.
conflicts.hypothesis: Hypothesis: the observation adds bills not in the table (the table includes bills the Auditor-General classed as eligible). Not confirmed.
conflicts.effect: The roll-forward and the chart use the table (705.38), whose columns add up; the observation value is listed here.

conflicts.measure: Pending bills at 30 June 2025, County Executive, within the FY 2024/25 report

values.label: Controller of Budget FY 2024/25 report, Table 3.457, closing column (PDF p. 478, printed p. 435, RapidOCR)
Same report, text before Table 3.458 ("Kshs.1.12 billion"), whose ageing totals equal the opening stock of 1,123.65 (PDF p. 478)

conflicts.definitions: Same report, same date. Table 3.457 gives 1,123.65 at 1 July 2024 less 577.70 paid, with the column for new bills left blank; the text and the ageing table give 1.12 billion.
conflicts.hypothesis: Hypothesis: the ageing table was not updated after payments, or new bills of the year were left out of Table 3.457. Not confirmed.
conflicts.effect: The FY 2024/25 year-end stock stays out of the chart, as before. The roll-forward shows the table value with this register case; the year is incomplete because new bills are not published.
